semantics.state: one stored input sample and registered output
semantics.transition: At rising edge n: stored_sample := a sampled at edge n; q := complement of stored_sample from before edge n. Thus q[n] = ~a[n-1] after nonblocking updates.
semantics.reset: No reset port or reset behavior
semantics.initialization: No explicit initialization; stored sample and q initially unknown in four-state simulation. First rising edge leaves q unknown; second edge resolves q if first sample was known.
semantics.waveform: Samples 0 at 5ns give q=1 at 15ns; sample 1 at 35ns gives q=0 at 45ns.

numeric.unknowns: Complement of x or z produces x
numeric.arithmetic: No arithmetic, overflow, rounding, truncation or signed interpretation

verification.oracle: Maintain a history of driven rising-edge input samples; expected q is complement of preceding sample, with initial expected x. Compare after NBA settling using case inequality.
verification.directed: Reproduce supplied waveform with inputs stable before sampling edges; check initial unknown, first edge unknown, subsequent ones then zeros.
verification.additional: Exercise alternating bits, consecutive equal bits, all length-four binary sequences, x/z samples, and input changes away from rising edges. Check q holds on falling edges and between edges.
verification.tools: Icarus Verilog v12, -g2012, explicit dev_tb top, finite compile and simulation timeouts

specification_ambiguities: The finite waveform cannot uniquely specify every possible sequential circuit. Adopt the minimal two-register delayed-inversion circuit consistent with the first-edge unknown and one-cycle delayed response.
Input changes are listed at clock rising-edge timestamps; development tests establish inputs before those edges to avoid simulator scheduling races.
